## Summary

`_reads._tracker` raises `store_uninitialized` only when the tracker directory is ABSENT
(`src/rebar/_reads.py`, `if not os.path.isdir(tracker)`). A directory that EXISTS but is not a
usable store — no `.git`, or a `.git` with no resolvable HEAD, or one mid-clone — satisfies
`isdir`, so every read returns `[]`. The caller cannot distinguish "this store is empty" from
"this store is broken", which is the exact confusion the guard was added to remove.

## Encountered three times, each independently

1. **In production.** The deployed MCP server served an EMPTY tracker for an extended period.
   The store dir held `reviewbot-ensure-tickets` marker files and no `.git` at all; `isdir` was
   true, so the guard never fired and `rebar.list_tickets()` returned `READ_OK count=0`. Proven
   on the box before repair.
2. **`fathomable-yester-thrip` (change 2244, merged).** `clear_tracker_dir` empties the
   directory's CONTENTS but leaves the directory, so between the clear and a completed clone
   reads return `[]`. Recorded there as a residual rather than fixed.
3. **`unfit-beneficial-whimbrel` AC3.** "While the clone is in flight, tracker reads report
   `store_uninitialized` rather than `[]`" — NOT met, for the same reason. That AC is
   explicitly left unticked and points here.

## Why the obvious fixes do not apply

The MCP deployment's tracker path is itself a MOUNT POINT (`/dev/nvme1n1`, xfs, verified in
`/proc/mounts`), so the directory cannot be removed and nothing can be renamed over it — which
is why the entrypoint clears contents rather than the directory. The fix has to be on the READ
side.

## Constraint the fix must respect

An EXISTING but empty INITIALIZED store must still read `[]` — that is a real contract with an
existing test (`tests/unit/test_reads_uninitialized_store.py`: "An EXISTING but empty store is
NOT an error"). So the discriminator cannot be emptiness. It has to be "is this a usable
store": rebar's own `.env-id` initialization marker and/or a resolvable git HEAD. Note the
related inconsistency already filed as `ab61-f3e8-6ee6-4905` (`comment` succeeds without
`.env-id` while `create` fails), which suggests `.env-id` is the intended marker.

## Blast radius

`_reads._tracker` funnels 7 read entry points, so this changes core read semantics repo-wide.
That is why it was scoped out of 2244 rather than folded in.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A tracker directory that exists but is NOT a usable store reads as `store_uninitialized`,
      not `[]`.
- [ ] An existing, empty, INITIALIZED store still reads `[]` — the existing contract test
      continues to pass unmodified.
- [ ] A store mid-clone (directory present, HEAD not yet resolvable) reads as uninitialized.
- [ ] Regression coverage fails if the predicate reverts to a bare `os.path.isdir`.

---

## Fix plan (operator-APPROVED; rebar-debug Phase 1 -> Phase 2; rev2 after plan-review BLOCK)

**Root cause (proven, cited).** `_reads._tracker()` (`src/rebar/_reads.py`) gates the read
path on `os.path.isdir(tracker)` only. A directory that exists but is not a usable store
(no `.git`, or `.git` present with an unresolvable HEAD mid-clone) satisfies `isdir`, so the
guard never fires and the reducer's `except OSError: return results` yields `[]`. Attributed
to `44fd-230c-5893-4246` (introducing commit `84fc5f9b`). Full RCA in the prior comment.

**Approved change (read-SEMANTICS change; scoped out of change 2244 on purpose).** Broaden
the read-side init predicate so a present-but-unusable store raises `store_uninitialized`
instead of returning `[]`, across all library/MCP read entry points (the ~7 that funnel
through `_reads._tracker`; the MCP agent read surface delegates to these library facades).
Read predicate: `.git` present AND `git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD` resolves.

**The read/write init gates, precisely (addresses plan-review BLOCK f4133576).** There are
THREE init-related gates and they are deliberately NOT all identical:
- `event_prepare._ensure_initialized` (`src/rebar/_store/event_prepare.py`) -- a `.git`-presence
  check on the low-level append path.
- `_seam.append_event` (`src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:555`) -- the AUTHORITATIVE write-command
  init gate, which requires `.env-id` (the provenance stamp; bug roar-nurse-stomp / ab61).
- the read chokepoint `_reads._tracker` -- being broadened here.

Reads DELIBERATELY do NOT adopt the `.env-id` predicate: `.env-id` is git-ignored LOCAL state,
absent immediately after a valid clone, yet a just-cloned store (HEAD resolves) MUST be
readable before its local `.env-id` is written (verified in-session: a store with HEAD +
`.git` but no `.env-id` reads its tickets, while a write is correctly rejected by the `_seam`
gate). So this change does NOT claim full read/write parity across all gates -- writes still
require `.env-id` and reads intentionally do not. What it DOES do is close the specific
`.git`/HEAD disagreement that caused THIS bug: a broken or mid-clone store that the write path
would reject but reads silently reported as empty. The shared predicate unifies the read guard
with the `.git`-presence base of `event_prepare._ensure_initialized` and strengthens both with
HEAD resolution.

**Design.** Factor a SHARED usability predicate into a new stdlib-only leaf
`src/rebar/_store/store_usability.py::store_is_usable(tracker)` = isdir AND `.git` present AND
`git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD` resolves. Both the read chokepoint (`_reads._tracker`) and the
low-level write guard (`event_prepare._ensure_initialized`) call it. The explicit `.git`-exists
check precedes the HEAD probe so git cannot walk UP to the parent code repo and resolve the
WRONG HEAD. A stdlib-only leaf keeps `_reads` out of the import SCC (no rebar back-edges).

**Files.**
- `src/rebar/_store/store_usability.py` (new) -- shared `store_is_usable` predicate.
- `src/rebar/_reads.py` -- `_tracker` raises `store_uninitialized` when `not store_is_usable`.
- `src/rebar/_store/event_prepare.py` -- `_ensure_initialized` calls the shared predicate.
- `tests/unit/test_reads_uninitialized_store.py` -- regression cases below.

**Caller-dependency gate (verified).** The ONLY consumer of the `store_uninitialized` code is
`rebar.audit.server._audited_tickets`, which catches exactly that code and degrades to an empty
web index while propagating every other error -- so broadening the guard keeps it safe (empty
page, not 500). No caller depends on the old `[]`-for-broken-store behaviour.

**Acceptance criteria.**
- [ ] A tracker dir that exists but is NOT a usable store (no `.git`) reads as
      `store_uninitialized`, not `[]`.
- [ ] A store mid-clone (`.git` present, HEAD not resolvable) reads as `store_uninitialized`.
- [ ] An existing, empty, INITIALIZED store still reads `[]` (existing contract test unchanged).
- [ ] A valid clone with a resolvable HEAD but NO `.env-id` still READS successfully (does not
      over-reject) -- reads and writes deliberately differ on `.env-id`.
- [ ] Regression coverage fails if the predicate reverts to a bare `os.path.isdir`.

**Verification (observable, in-session -- addresses G6 coaching).** Success is proven by the
RED->GREEN test in `tests/unit/test_reads_uninitialized_store.py`: the broken-store and
mid-clone cases are seen RED (return `[]`) before the fix and GREEN (raise `store_uninitialized`)
after; the empty-initialized-store and no-`.env-id`-clone cases stay GREEN (`[]`) throughout;
and a defect-seeded mutation reverting the predicate to bare `os.path.isdir` returns the broken
and mid-clone cases to RED. Full suite (`make test` subset for reads + writes) stays green.

**Out of approved scope (parity -- discovered tickets, not expanded here):** the CLI read path
(`reads_cli.py`) and other bare-`isdir` sites -- assessed in the Step 7 parity sweep.
